source_text: Fratrem domum tuam introgressum ne sine oratione dimiseris (uidisti, inquit, fratrem, uidisti dominum tuum), maxime aduenam, ne angelus forte sit. sed nec ipse a fratribus exceptus priora fecerit refrigeria terrena caelestibus. statim enim iudicabitur fides tua. aut quomodo secundum praeceptum pax huic domui dices, nisi et eis qui in domo sunt pacem mutuam reddas?
thought_title: Greeting a brother with prayer and peace
orientation: Tertullian is giving practical rules for prayer in daily life, now about how to receive a brother who enters your house.
pass_a_gloss: Do not send away a brother who has entered your house without prayer. You have seen, he says, a brother; you have seen your Lord. Especially a stranger, lest he perhaps be an angel. But do not you yourself, received by brothers, put earthly refreshments before heavenly ones. For immediately your faith will be judged. Or how will you say according to the command, Peace to this house, unless you also return mutual peace to those who are in the house?

pass_b_english: Do not send a brother away without prayer when he has entered your house. “You have seen,” he says, “a brother; you have seen your Lord”—especially if he is a stranger, lest he perhaps be an angel. But neither should you yourself, when received by brothers, put earthly refreshments before heavenly ones. For your faith will be judged immediately. Or how will you say “Peace to this house” according to the command (Matthew 10:12-13), unless you also return mutual peace to those who are in the house?
